nodes.summary: Let $C$ and $m$ be natural numbers with $m > 0$ and $m \mid C$. Then for every natural number $j$, $\lfloor C(j + 18900)/(18900m) \rfloor = \lfloor Cj/(18900m) \rfloor + C/m$.
nodes.title: Shifting a floor quotient by one period

nodes.summary: Let $C$ and $L$ be positive natural numbers, let $m$ be a divisor of $210$ with $C \mid mL$, and let $x \ge 0$ be a real number. Then $\lfloor Cx/m \rfloor = \lfloor C \lfloor Lx \rfloor / (mL) \rfloor$.
nodes.title: Real floors at divisors of 210 agree with grid floors

nodes.summary: For every natural number $j$, the grid $G$-function for $k = 9$ satisfies $G_9(j + 18900) = G_9(j)$.
nodes.title: One-period shift of $G_9$

nodes.summary: For every natural number $n \ge 4762$, $13n - 16 - 48\log(2100n) - \sqrt{2100n}\,\log(2100n) > 0$, where $\log$ is the natural logarithm.
nodes.title: Positivity of the gap in Breusch's prime interval argument

nodes.summary: Let $a$ and $t$ be real numbers with $a > 0$, $t > 1$ and $\log a > 2$, where $\log$ is the natural logarithm. Then $\frac{\log(at)}{\sqrt{at}} < \frac{\log a}{\sqrt{a}}$.
nodes.title: Strict decay of log over square root beyond e squared

nodes.summary: For every real number $x \ge 10^7$, $\log x \le 0.006\sqrt{x}$, where $\log$ is the natural logarithm.
nodes.title: Logarithm bounded by a multiple of the square root

nodes.summary: The natural logarithm satisfies $\log 10 = \log 2 + \log 5$.
nodes.title: Logarithm of 10

nodes.summary: The natural logarithm of $17$ satisfies $\log 17 < 2.8333$.

nodes.summary: The natural logarithm satisfies $\log(34/10) = \log 17 - \log 5$.
nodes.title: Logarithm of 3.4

nodes.summary: The natural logarithm satisfies $\log 9 = 2 \log 3$.
nodes.title: Logarithm of 9

nodes.summary: For all natural numbers $a$ and $b$, the floor of the real number $a / b$ equals the quotient of $a$ by $b$ in integer division. When $b = 0$ both sides are $0$, since division by zero gives $0$ in both the reals and the natural numbers.
nodes.title: Floor of a quotient of natural numbers

nodes.summary: Let $a$, $b$, $d$ be natural numbers with $b > 0$, $d > 0$, $d \mid b$ and $d \mid a$. Then the remainder of $a$ modulo $b$ is at most $b - d$.
nodes.title: Remainder bound for common multiples

nodes.summary: Let $\pi(m)$ denote the number of primes $p \le m$. For every natural number $m \ge 156$, $3\pi(m) \le m$.
nodes.title: Prime-counting bound $\pi(m) \le m/3$ from $156$ on

nodes.summary: Let $\pi(m)$ denote the number of primes $p \le m$. For every natural number $m \ge 36$, $3\pi(m) \le m$.
nodes.title: Prime-counting bound $\pi(m) \le m/3$ for natural $m \ge 36$

nodes.summary: Let $\pi(m)$ denote the number of primes $p \le m$. For every natural number $m$ with $36 \le m < 156$, $3\pi(m) \le m$.
nodes.title: Prime-counting bound $\pi(m) \le m/3$ for $36 \le m < 156$

nodes.summary: Let $\pi(n)$ denote the number of primes $p \le n$. For every real number $x \ge 36$, $\pi(\lfloor x \rfloor) \le x/3$.
nodes.title: Prime-counting bound $\pi(x) \le x/3$ for real $x \ge 36$

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
